judgements.reason: Bridge->Reasoning, and the premise the whole thesis rests on broke this week. The prediction is framed on Samsung being 'the one large memory maker absent from this week's capital surge' facing pressure 'to signal its own capacity path rather than cede the narrative'. validation.5c1dc15555584996 (07-30, rel 4, support_dimension landing) reports Samsung's Q2 release -- consolidated revenue KRW 171.5tn, operating profit KRW 89.5tn, Device Solutions KRW 89.2tn operating profit, record share of server revenue, HBM4 scaling, industry-first HBM4E samples -- and states flatly 'There is no new fab, no expanded line, no raised memory capital-expenditure figure and no capacity target anywhere in it', closing with 'Samsung is the most profitable of the three suppliers now, not the conspicuously absent one'. Samsung answered the scarcity with contracting instead: 60-70% of capacity under long-term agreement, which the bridge calls 'the opposite move to adding new ones'. reasoning_because (Micron's $250bn raise plus SK Hynix's EUV-earmarked listing, 2026-07-09) stays true as history; what must be rewritten is reasoning_given and reasoning_so_that, which assume an absence and a competitive-shame motive that a record quarter and a contracting strategy have removed. Retire is premature -- the Q3 (late October) and Q4 releases fall inside the Q1 2027 window -- but the rewrite must state the new falsifier: Samsung may satisfy demand by allocation rather than by capex, in which case the prediction fails without any contrary announcement ever appearing.
